request:
Our school library wants a simple catalogue of its books. The librarian should be able to add a book with its title, its author and how many copies the library owns. Students should be able to see all the books, and look at one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name, and returns it when they are done; a student can only return a book they actually borrowed. When every copy of a book is out, nobody else can borrow it until a copy comes back.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Should adding books be restricted to the librarian (for example with a password), or is it fine if anyone using the system can add a book?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Is there a limit on how many books one student can borrow at the same time, and can a student borrow more than one copy of the same book?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Do loans need a due date (for example, 2 weeks), with overdue books shown, or do we only track who has which book?
A: Not needed for now.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).

plan.summary: This plan sets up a simple catalogue for your school library. Anyone using the system can add a book with its title, its author and how many copies the library owns. Students can see every book and look at one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name and returns it the same way. The system keeps track of who has which copy, so a student can only return a book they actually borrowed, and a book cannot be borrowed once every copy is out. Where you had no preference, we chose the simplest option. Adding books is open to anyone, with no password. There is no limit on how many books a student can borrow. A student may borrow more than one copy of the same book, as long as copies are on the shelf. As you asked, there are no due dates and no overdue lists. Some questions for you to consider, which are not included in this plan: Should students' names be kept private, so that only the librarian can see who borrowed what? Should books be editable or removable after they are added? Two students with exactly the same name would be treated as the same person. Is that acceptable, or should students give something extra to tell them apart?

data.name: Book
fields: Book number (given automatically, used to pick out one book)
Number of copies the library owns
Number of copies still on the shelf (worked out from copies owned minus copies currently borrowed)

data.name: Loan (one borrowed copy)
fields: Name of the student who borrowed it

endpoints.does: Adds a new book to the catalogue, using its title, its author and how many copies the library owns.
Shows every book in the catalogue with its title and author.
Shows one book: its title, its author, how many copies the library owns and how many are still on the shelf.
A student borrows one copy of this book by giving their name. One fewer copy is then on the shelf.
A student returns one copy of this book by giving their name. One more copy is then back on the shelf.

rules: A book cannot be added without a title and an author.
The number of copies must be a whole number and cannot be below zero.
Borrowing or returning is refused if the student does not give a name.
Borrowing or returning is refused if the book does not exist in the catalogue.
Borrowing is refused when every copy of the book is already out, until a copy comes back.
A return is refused if that student does not currently have a copy of that book borrowed.

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app import app


@pytest.fixture
def client():
    with TestClient(app) as c:
        yield c


def add(client, title="Matilda", author="Roald Dahl", copies=2):
    r = client.post("/books", json={"title": title, "author": author, "copies": copies})
    assert r.status_code == 201, r.text
    return r.json()


def test_add_and_get_book(client):
    b = add(client)
    assert b["title"] == "Matilda" and b["author"] == "Roald Dahl"
    assert b["copies"] == 2 and b["on_shelf"] == 2
    r = client.get(f"/books/{b['id']}")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json()["on_shelf"] == 2


def test_list_books(client):
    b = add(client, title="Holes", author="Louis Sachar")
    r = client.get("/books")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    found = [x for x in r.json() if x["id"] == b["id"]]
    assert found and found[0]["title"] == "Holes" and found[0]["author"] == "Louis Sachar"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("body", [
    {"author": "A", "copies": 1},
    {"title": "T", "copies": 1},
    {"title": "  ", "author": "A", "copies": 1},
    {"title": "T", "author": "", "copies": 1},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies": -1},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies": 2.5},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies": "two"},
    {"title": "T", "author": "A"},
])
def test_add_book_invalid(client, body):
    assert client.post("/books", json=body).status_code == 422


def test_zero_copies_allowed_but_cannot_borrow(client):
    b = add(client, copies=0)
    r = client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/borrow", json={"name": "Ann"})
    assert r.status_code == 409


def test_missing_book(client):
    assert client.get("/books/999999").status_code == 404
    assert client.post("/books/999999/borrow", json={"name": "Ann"}).status_code == 404
    assert client.post("/books/999999/return", json={"name": "Ann"}).status_code == 404


def test_borrow_and_return_flow(client):
    b = add(client, copies=2)
    bid = b["id"]
    r = client.post(f"/books/{bid}/borrow", json={"name": "Ann"})
    assert r.status_code == 201
    assert client.get(f"/books/{bid}").json()["on_shelf"] == 1
    # same student may borrow a second copy
    assert client.post(f"/books/{bid}/borrow", json={"name": "Ann"}).status_code == 201
    assert client.get(f"/books/{bid}").json()["on_shelf"] == 0
    # all out
    assert client.post(f"/books/{bid}/borrow", json={"name": "Ben"}).status_code == 409
    # Ben never borrowed it
    assert client.post(f"/books/{bid}/return", json={"name": "Ben"}).status_code == 409
    # Ann returns one
    r = client.post(f"/books/{bid}/return", json={"name": "Ann"})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"/books/{bid}").json()["on_shelf"] == 1
    # now Ben can borrow
    assert client.post(f"/books/{bid}/borrow", json={"name": "Ben"}).status_code == 201
    assert client.post(f"/books/{bid}/return", json={"name": "Ben"}).status_code == 200
    assert client.post(f"/books/{bid}/return", json={"name": "Ann"}).status_code == 200
    # Ann has none left
    assert client.post(f"/books/{bid}/return", json={"name": "Ann"}).status_code == 409
    assert client.get(f"/books/{bid}").json()["on_shelf"] == 2


def test_return_only_for_that_book(client):
    a = add(client, title="A")
    b = add(client, title="B")
    client.post(f"/books/{a['id']}/borrow", json={"name": "Cara"})
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/return", json={"name": "Cara"}).status_code == 409


@pytest.mark.parametrize("body", [{}, {"name": ""}, {"name": "   "}])
def test_name_required(client, body):
    b = add(client)
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/borrow", json=body).status_code == 422
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/return", json=body).status_code == 422

I've built the library catalogue in one file, `app.py`, and all 17 automated checks pass. The data is saved in a file called `library.db` in the same folder.

**What the system can do:**
- **POST /books** adds a book. You send its title, its author and the number of copies the library owns, and you get back the new book with its book number.
- **GET /books** lists every book with its title and author, plus how many copies the library owns and how many are on the shelf.
- **GET /books/{book number}** shows one book: its title, its author, how many copies the library owns and how many are still on the shelf.
- **POST /books/{book number}/borrow** lends out one copy. The student sends their name.
- **POST /books/{book number}/return** takes back one copy. The student sends their name.

**Requests the system refuses:**
- **Adding a book** is refused if the title or author is missing or blank, or if the number of copies isn't a whole number of zero or more.
- **Borrowing or returning** is refused if the student's name is missing or blank, or if the book doesn't exist.
- **Borrowing** is refused when every copy is out.
- **Returning** is refused if that student doesn't currently have a copy of that book.

**Choices made where you had no preference:**
- **Adding books** is open to anyone, with no password.
- **Borrowing limits:** there's no limit on how many books a student can borrow. A student can also borrow more than one copy of the same book while copies are on the shelf.
- **Zero copies:** a book can be added with 0 copies, and nobody can borrow it.
- **Names** are matched exactly, so "Ann" and "ann" count as different students. As the plan said, two students with the same name count as the same person.
